findings.title: Container running as privileged
findings.description: A privileged container has full access to the host, bypassing almost all isolation. Privilege is almost never required for application containers.
findings.remediation:
Drop privileged mode. Remove `securityContext.privileged: true` and use the
minimum Linux capabilities the container needs:
securityContext:
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  runAsNonRoot: true
  capabilities:
    drop: ["ALL"]
Enforce with Pod Security Standards (restricted) or Kyverno/OPA policies.

findings.title: Container running as root user
findings.description: Containers should run as a non-root user. An explicit runAsNonRoot: false or runAsUser: 0 keeps the container root, magnifying the impact of a container escape.

evidence.expected: runAsUser set to a non-zero UID

findings.remediation: Enable MFA on the account and restrict root usage. Create individual IAM users or federate via SSO, attach least-privilege policies, and never use root for daily operations.

findings.title: Container without resource limits
findings.description: A container without resources.limits for cpu and memory can exhaust node resources (noisy neighbor / DoS). Set cpu and memory limits on every container.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Pod with hostNetwork enabled
findings.description: A pod with hostNetwork: true shares the node's network namespace, bypassing network policies and exposing host ports. Avoid hostNetwork.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Container without liveness probe
findings.description: A container without a livenessProbe is never restarted when it deadlocks, leaving a broken pod serving traffic. Define a liveness probe.
findings.remediation: Review the flagged configuration against AWS security best practices and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark. Apply the control the rule describes, preferring restrictive defaults, encryption, and audit logging. Validate with `aegis scan` after the change.

findings.title: Container without readiness probe
findings.description: A container without a readinessProbe receives traffic before it is ready, causing failed requests during startup. Define a readiness probe.
